brief: Goldman's mid-day color frames today as reversion from yesterday's violent de-grossing event, the 5th largest this year at -1.6 SD, driven entirely by long selling (largest since September 2025) across 9 of 11 sectors, with info tech seeing the largest net selling since September 2024 from long selling plus short additions. Today's bounce: the Momentum factor (GSPRHIMO) is +2.4% after closing -8% yesterday and erasing YTD gains; Goldman's HF positioning pair (GSTHVIPP) is +38bps after its worst move since 2011 (-4.2% yesterday); the Nasdaq 100 is +30bps after its worst day since mid-June; the AI basket (GSTMTAIP) is +45bps after finishing -6% yesterday, still down 23% from June highs. Breadth stays weak (over 70% of SPX red), volumes are muted, liquidity is challenged (Top of Book -17% vs 5dma), and CTAs are forecast to sell in all tape scenarios next week. Brent crude is above $117/bbl on Middle East tensions. Desk flows (HFs and LOs) remain skewed for sale. Next week brings heavy event risk: 44% of the S&P reports, including GOOGL/MSFT (Wed) and AMZN (Thu), plus the Fed's rate decision Wednesday.
